name: Snowdrop Voice Search
author: snowdropsignals

sections.description:
Snowdrop Voice Search helps WordPress posts and articles become better prepared for voice search, AI assistants, and smart-device discovery.

People now search by talking to Google, AI assistants, phones, cars, speakers, and smart devices. Your article should have one clear short summary that explains what it is about.

Snowdrop Voice Search lets you add that summary in the post editor and uses it as a quiet structured-data layer for the article. It does not add a repeated block inside the article and does not interrupt the reader experience.

Think of it like a neon sign for voice search: instead of leaving search and AI systems to guess which part of your article matters most, the plugin gives them one clear summary of the post.

This may help search and AI systems understand, surface, or reference your content more easily. It does not guarantee rankings, traffic, citations, or sales.

What it does:
– adds a Snowdrop Voice Summary field to posts
– keeps the summary out of the visible article layout
– outputs Article structured data on single post pages when a summary exists
– uses the summary as Article description and abstract data
– adds a Speakable-style reference to a Snowdrop voice-summary meta target
– adds a character counter and simple summary quality guidance
– adds a Voice Summary status column to the Posts list
– adds a basic Voice Readiness dashboard under Posts
– works alongside SEO, AEO, and LLMO plugins without replacing them

Best for:
– bloggers
– recipe sites
– news sites
– small publishers
– magazine-style WordPress sites
– businesses with active blog content
– WooCommerce stores with an active blog

What it is not:
– a full SEO plugin
– a product page schema plugin
– a voice-search box for visitors
– a text-to-speech audio player
– an automatic AI writing tool
– a guarantee of rankings, traffic, citations, or sales
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to the /wp-content/plugins/snowdrop-voice-search directory, or install the plugin through the WordPress plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress.
  3. Open a post in the editor.
  4. Enter a short Snowdrop Voice Summary in the side panel.
  5. Publish or update the post.
  6. Use Posts > Voice Readiness to see which posts have summaries and which still need work.
sections.faq:
Does this replace my SEO plugin?

No. Snowdrop Voice Search is a focused helper for voice and AI discovery. It does not replace SEO plugins and does not edit your SEO title, meta description, canonical URL, social tags, sitemaps, or existing SEO plugin settings.

Will it show extra text inside my article?

No. Version 0.2.0 no longer adds a visible summary block to the article. The summary is used for structured data and discovery markup only.

Does it work with SEO, AEO, or LLMO plugins?

Yes. Snowdrop Voice Search is designed to work alongside those tools. It adds its own focused voice-summary markup only when a post has a Snowdrop Voice Summary.

Does it work on product pages?

No. This version is for WordPress posts only. It can help WooCommerce stores that publish active blog content, but it does not add product-page schema.

Does it automatically create the summary?

No. In this version, you add the summary manually. The plugin gives a character counter, simple feedback, and examples to help you write a stronger summary.

What is the Voice Summary column?

The Posts list includes a Voice Summary column that shows whether each post is ready, missing a summary, too short, or too long.

What is the Voice Readiness dashboard?

The dashboard gives a simple overview of total posts, ready posts, posts missing summaries, and posts that need review.

Will this increase rankings, traffic, citations, or sales?

No plugin can guarantee rankings, traffic, citations, or sales. Snowdrop Voice Search helps your posts become better prepared for voice and AI discovery.

Is it easy to remove?

Yes. The plugin is designed to be small and lightweight.
sections.changelog:
0.2.0

  • Removed the visible front-end summary block from posts.
  • Kept the Snowdrop Voice Summary as an editor/admin field only.
  • Added Snowdrop voice-summary metadata in the page head.
  • Added Article structured data using the voice summary as description and abstract.
  • Updated Speakable-style output to use a Snowdrop voice-summary xPath target instead of a visible article block selector.
  • Added a live character counter in the post editor.
  • Added simple summary quality guidance: missing, too short, good length, or too long.
  • Added example summaries for recipes, news, and guide-style posts.
  • Added a Voice Summary status column to the Posts list.
  • Added a basic Voice Readiness dashboard under Posts.
  • Improved compatibility with SEO, AEO, and LLMO plugins by not changing their titles, meta descriptions, canonicals, social tags, sitemaps, or settings.

0.1.1

  • Renamed plugin to Snowdrop Voice Search.
  • Updated slug and text domain to snowdrop-voice-search.
  • Improved JSON-LD output by using wp_json_encode without extra unescaped flags.

0.1.0

  • First public release.
  • Manual summary field for posts.
  • Front-end summary display on single posts.
  • Article schema output with SpeakableSpecification.
